questions: Does the automated (RazorpayX gateway) payout path ever call a Payout factory method that accepts a tdsAmount, or is tdsAmount only ever supplied on the admin manual-payout path?

Is there ANY user-facing surface (creator wallet, invoices, tax documents tab) that states TDS is being withheld as a fact, and does that claim match what the backend actually computes on the automated path?
Does a backend endpoint exist anywhere to generate/serve a Form 16A document, or is that purely a frontend copy promise with nothing behind it?
Is AdminFinanceService's tdsAmount a computed value (rate x amount) or an admin-typed free-form number with only a sanity-range check?
What is the actual WCAG contrast ratio of --hype-solid (#06b6d4 light / #22d3ee dark) against white, computed independently rather than trusted from the finder's number?
Is --hype-solid actually rendered as TEXT on a white background anywhere in the codebase, or is its only real usage as a button/badge BACKGROUND paired with white text?
If hype-solid is only used as a background, does the white-text-on-hype-solid pairing have the same or a different contrast ratio than the text-on-white framing the finder used?
Which live, reachable UI surfaces actually render bg-hype-solid (hero CTA, campaign cards, inbox actions), and does the contrast failure hold in both light and dark theme variants?

Does AffiliateSettlementWriter's creditCreatorWallet() post a single ledger leg (clearing wallet -> creator wallet) or is there a second, compensating leg elsewhere in the affiliate pipeline that debits a brand wallet?

Is the platform clearing wallet's exemption from the non-negative-balance check (WalletLedgerService) documented/intended to cover the affiliate-commission debit case, or was it built for an unrelated scenario (brand top-up timing lag) and merely happens to also apply here?
Does any job or alert monitor the clearing wallet's balance for drift caused specifically by affiliate commission settlement, as opposed to top-up/payout reconciliation?

Is CommissionInvoiceService (which also references commissionAmount) actually wired to the affiliate program, or is it an unrelated platform take-rate/GST invoicing feature that could be mistaken for a brand-debit mechanism?

Does this affiliate-commission funding gap relate to, or contradict, the existing project memory note that affiliate commission 'has NEVER been credited' (a prior audit describing the opposite failure mode)?

verdicts.reason: Independently opened Payout.java at the RC: tdsAmount (line 84-85) defaults to null and is set ONLY inside createManualPaid (line 218/235), which requires a human-supplied bankReference and tdsAmount and is never called from any automated flow. createPending (lines 129-151, the pre-gateway-call factory) and createQueued (lines 165-189, used both for milestone payouts and wallet withdrawals) take NO tdsAmount parameter at all. Confirmed both real call sites: PayoutService.java:463 calls Payout.createPending (automated escrow-milestone payout path) and WalletService.java:402 calls Payout.createQueued (creator wallet withdrawal path) -- neither can ever populate tdsAmount. The only caller of createManualPaid is AdminFinanceService.java:230, fed by AdminFinanceController.java:103 / body.tdsAmount() -- an admin-typed number with only a range sanity check (AdminFinanceService.java:179-183), not a computed 1% withholding. This independently corroborates the finder's location and mechanism exactly. Went beyond the cited files and found a second, more concrete instance of the same defect: src/pages/creator-wallet.tsx:978 renders to every creator, as a flat present-tense factual claim, 'TDS (1%) is deducted at source as per IT Act. Download Form 16A quarterly for filing.' -- directly above (lines 982-990) an admitted empty state ('No tax-document endpoint exists yet... No tax documents yet') in the SAME tab. Grepped the entire influora-api tree for Form16A/form16a and found zero backend implementation anywhere -- the download promise has nothing behind it. This means the finder's claim is not just plausible but understated: it isn't only that copy 'implies' automatic withholding, one screen states it as settled fact while the code immediately below contradicts it, for every creator paid through the only payout paths that exist at scale (gateway milestone payout, wallet withdrawal). The 'fix wave 0828 / CA-gate' disagreement note explains why automatic TDS computation was descoped from engineering, but does not justify or excuse shipping a hardcoded UI claim that it already happens -- that gap is exactly what the finder flagged as 'the defect is the claim,' and I confirm it independently. No runtime execution performed (this is a static UI/entity/service read, not a call I could safely exercise without a live payout), so evidence stays at E3 rather than E4.
verdicts.new_evidence: src/pages/creator-wallet.tsx:978 states 'TDS (1%) is deducted at source as per IT Act. Download Form 16A quarterly for filing' as a factual claim, directly contradicted by the same tab's own empty-state copy ('No tax-document endpoint exists yet') and by the absence of any Form16A generation code anywhere in influora-api -- a second, independently-found instance of the same misrepresentation the finder described.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed globals.css:101 defines --hype-solid: #06b6d4 (light theme) and line 171 defines --hype-solid: #22d3ee for dark theme. Independently recomputed the WCAG 2.x relative-luminance/contrast formula for #06b6d4 against white by hand: linear R=0.00182, G=0.46812, B=0.65861 -> relative luminance L=0.38276 -> contrast ratio (1.05)/(0.38276+0.05)=2.426:1 -- this matches the finder's cited 2.43:1 almost exactly, an independent reproduction of the number rather than a trust of the claim. That ratio fails WCAG AA for normal text (4.5:1) and even the lower AA large-text/non-text-UI-component threshold (3:1). HOWEVER, grepping every real usage of hype-solid in src/**/*.tsx (8 call sites) found NO instance of hype-solid used as literal foreground TEXT color on a white/light background anywhere in the shipped UI -- the finder's specific framing ('Hype solid color on white') does not correspond to any code that exists. Every real usage is either `bg-hype-solid text-white` (landing.tsx:503 hero CTA button, hype-inbox-card.tsx:95, FunnelCta.tsx:81, brand-new-hype-campaign.tsx:646) or non-text decoration (focus ring, pulse dot, progress-bar fill). Because WCAG contrast ratio is symmetric regardless of which color is foreground vs background, the identical 2.43:1 failure applies to the ACTUAL shipped pairing: white button-label text on a hype-solid background. I additionally computed the dark-mode variant (#22d3ee vs white text) independently: L=0.53102 -> ratio (1.05)/(0.58102)=1.807:1, an even worse failure. Net result: the underlying accessibility defect is real, reachable in production on multiple live brand CTAs (landing hero button, hype campaign card, creator hype-inbox action button, brand hype-campaign creation flow) in BOTH light and dark themes, but the finder's stated mechanism (text-on-white) is not what's in the code -- it is white-text-on-hype-solid-background, an equally real but differently-described failure. I am not downgrading severity or confidence below the original because the corrected mechanism is, if anything, more clearly and more broadly reachable (real buttons on the live homepage) than a bare CSS-token comparison. Static analysis only (evidence_score 3, no browser-rendered contrast tool run), consistent with the rubric note that static-only findings should rarely exceed ~85 confidence.
verdicts.new_evidence: No code anywhere renders hype-solid AS TEXT on a white background; the real, reachable defect is white button-label text ON a hype-solid background (landing.tsx:503, hype-inbox-card.tsx:95, FunnelCta.tsx:81, brand-new-hype-campaign.tsx:646), which has the identical 2.43:1 (light) / ~1.81:1 (dark, independently computed for #22d3ee) contrast failure -- the finder's number is right, the color-role description is not.

verdicts.reason: Read AffiliateSettlementWriter.java's creditCreatorWallet() in full (lines 114-143): it posts exactly ONE walletLedgerService.post() call -- debit platformWalletService.requireClearingWallet(), credit walletService.requireOrCreateUserWallet(creatorId), for earning.getCommissionAmount() -- with WalletTransactionType.AFFILIATE_COMMISSION. There is no second/compensating posting in this method, in this class, or anywhere else: grepped all 20 files in the RC that reference AffiliateEarning (AffiliateEarningsService, AffiliateEarningRecordingListener, RedemptionWriter, CouponCodeService, AffiliateEarningReconciliationJob, etc.) for walletLedgerService/ledgerService/BrandWallet/debit and found zero hits outside this one writer. The only other file referencing 'commissionAmount' is CommissionInvoiceService.java, which I opened and confirmed is an unrelated feature (D14 Doc#3 platform take-rate/GST commission invoicing, wired into BrandCampaignFeeService#chargeOnPublish and PlatformFeeService#deductAtRelease for the PLATFORM's own fee, not the affiliate referral commission) -- ruling out a false-negative where a brand debit might be hiding under a similarly-named service. Confirmed WalletLedgerService.java:131-139 exactly as cited: the clearing wallet is explicitly exempted from the non-negative-balance invariant via debitWalletIsExemptPlatformAccount, so this debit is free to push the clearing wallet arbitrarily negative with no enforced floor. Read the surrounding comment (lines 120-130) and confirmed its stated rationale is a DIFFERENT scenario -- a brand's first top-up debiting the clearing wallet while Razorpay webhook confirmation is still pending (a bounded, self-correcting timing lag) -- with no mention of affiliate-commission funding; this strongly suggests the exemption's use here is an unintended side effect of a control built for a different purpose rather than a deliberate funding design for affiliate payouts. Found no job or check anywhere in the RC that monitors clearing-wallet balance health for the affiliate-settlement case specifically (AffiliateEarningReconciliationJob reconciles earning STATUS, not wallet balance; WalletTopUpReconciliationJob is scoped to top-ups). This is a genuine, structurally confirmed, silent and uncapped platform liability leak: every affiliate commission paid out is funded from an account with no corresponding revenue debit ever posted against the referring brand or campaign. Not executed at runtime (would require seeding a real coupon-redemption-to-settlement cycle); evidence rests on direct code reads across the full call graph, not a single file in isolation, which is why I did not downgrade evidence_score.
verdicts.new_evidence: The clearing-wallet negative-balance exemption's own code comment (WalletLedgerService.java:120-130) documents a rationale for a DIFFERENT scenario (brand top-up webhook timing lag) that says nothing about affiliate commissions -- suggesting AffiliateSettlementWriter's use of this exemption is an undocumented side effect, not an intentional funding design. This is a distinct area from the project memory note 'Affiliate settlement inert: two defects cancelling / commission has NEVER been credited' (opposite failure mode of commission never landing at all); worth reconciling which affiliate-path state the two audits each examined.
